core_obligations: Get the forward direction from the base change behaviour of irreducible components: geometric irreducibility of X makes the self product irreducible (proof lines 1493-1495).

For the converse, reduce X to its underlying reduced scheme, note that the first projection is surjective so X is irreducible and hence integral, and suppose there is alpha in the function field separably algebraic over k but not in k (proof lines 1498-1505).

Choose a nonempty affine open U with k contained in E = k(alpha) contained in O(U), obtain a dominant morphism U times U to Spec(E tensor E) from the inclusion into O(U) tensor O(U), and conclude that Spec(E tensor E) is connected; since E tensor E would be a product of at least two fields when E is bigger than k, deduce E = k and apply the function field criterion (proof lines 1508-1520).
proof_roadmap: Forward direction by base change of components (proof lines 1493-1495).
Reduce to X integral and assume a separably algebraic function (proof lines 1498-1505).
Use dominance to Spec(E tensor E) and the dimension count to force E = k (proof lines 1508-1520).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes geometric irreducibility of a scheme X over a field k by irreducibility of the self product X times_k X (statement lines 1486-1490). One direction is a consequence of the base change behaviour of irreducible components. The converse is the interesting half and runs by contradiction through the function field: after replacing X by its reduced structure one knows X is irreducible, hence integral; assuming there is a separably algebraic element alpha of the function field outside k, one chooses a nonempty affine open U with k contained in E = k(alpha) contained in O(U), so that E tensor_k E sits inside O(U times U) and one gets a dominant morphism to the spectrum of E tensor E; irreducibility of the self product then makes that spectrum connected (proof lines 1492-1512). But if E were bigger than k, its tensor square would be a product of at least two fields, since as a k-vector space it has dimension the square of dim_k(E), contradicting connectedness; hence E = k and the function field criterion gives geometric irreducibility (proof lines 1513-1520). The claim is H2: one reduction, one dominant-morphism argument and a short dimension count.
